project.name: Kincardine-on-Forth
project.boundarySource: National Records of Scotland Civil Parish Dataset (1930 civil-parish boundary; downloaded from NRS Geography Products).
project.researchNotes: The project extent is the official NRS Tulliallan civil-parish boundary. Kincardine-on-Forth is the historic town focus; conservation areas and other evidence layers are not substituted for the parish boundary.

townStudyArea.sourceName: National Records of Scotland 2022 Census Locality Boundaries
townStudyArea.notes: Modern statistical locality used only for the town listed-building register; it is not a historic boundary or a replacement for the project study boundary.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap current community places
sources.coverage: Cafés, picnic facilities, selected visitor points of interest and leisure places within the Kincardine study area plus its 500m buffer.
sources.accessMethod: Read-only Overpass API query, then exact point-in-study-area filtering and source-ID/name-proximity deduplication.
sources.licence: Open Database Licence (ODbL) v1.0; © OpenStreetMap contributors.
sources.limitations: Current voluntary mapping only. Tags, names and locations may change; this optional icon layer is excluded from historic evidence, dates, heat scoring, totals and historic exports.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap current parks and gardens
sources.coverage: Named leisure=park, leisure=garden and landuse=recreation_ground ways intersecting the Kincardine-on-Forth project boundary.
sources.accessMethod: OpenStreetMap API map call for the NRS locality plus 500m buffer; exact project-boundary intersection
sources.limitations: Current voluntary mapping only. It is not a historic park register, cannot establish dates or boundaries in the past, and is excluded from historic heat scoring.

sources.name: Historic Environment Scotland contextual datasets
sources.coverage: Exact project-boundary scan of local battlefields, Properties in Care, World Heritage Sites and Historic Marine Protected Areas for Kincardine-on-Forth.
sources.accessMethod: Developer-supplied local HES Shapefiles; exact project-boundary intersection
sources.licence: Open Government Licence v3.0; retain Historic Environment Scotland attribution and source link.
sources.limitations: A contextual designation or managed-property record is not construction-date evidence. Datasets with no intersecting records are retained as a completed scan, not shown as empty map layers.

sources.name: Historic Environment Scotland NRHE / trove.scot Points GIS
sources.coverage: NRHE records whose representative points lie within the authoritative Kincardine-on-Forth parish extent
sources.accessMethod: Developer-supplied local HES Shapefile; exact parish containment
sources.licence: Open Government Licence v3.0; retain Historic Environment Scotland attribution.
sources.limitations: The spatial index provides a representative site point, names and classifications. It does not establish construction dates; detailed source records require individual review.

sources.name: Historic Environment Scotland local designation Shapefiles
sources.accessMethod: Developer-supplied local HES Shapefiles; exact project-boundary intersection
sources.licence: Open Government Licence v3.0; retain Historic Environment Scotland attribution and source link.
sources.limitations: Includes statutory conservation-area, scheduled-monument and garden/designed-landscape polygons intersecting the NRS parish boundary. These are evidence layers, not construction dates or historic settlement footprints.

sources.name: Historic Environment Scotland Listed Buildings spatial data

features.name: 16 Forth Street, Railway Tavern
alternativeNames: Kincardine ferry, shoreline and minor port
Kincardine railway station and railway corridor
features.documentedDateText: Kincardine terminal opened 18 December 1893; wider Kincardine line developed in the early 20th century
features.shortDescription: A rare surviving small vernacular public house overlooking the Forth and associated with the historic ferry and railway.
features.fullDescription:
Historic Environment Scotland notes that a drovers' inn may have occupied the site before 1800 and that the North British Railway opened its Kincardine terminal on 18 December 1893.

The Railway Tavern designation links the site to the historic ferry and possible pre-1800 inn. Digitise landings and shorelines from verified maps.

Digitise station, goods yard, sidings and period-specific alignments from georeferenced Ordnance Survey mapping.

features.name: Tulliallan Castle Walled Garden, glasshouses and associated structures
alternativeNames: Walled Garden Including Glasshouses And Sundial, Tulliallan Castle
features.documentedDateText: Early-19th-century walled garden; principal glasshouses circa 1907
features.shortDescription: An extensive walled kitchen garden with rare and substantially intact early-20th-century horticultural glasshouses.
features.fullDescription:
Included as part of the comprehensive Kincardine and Tulliallan statutory inventory. The live HES record remains authoritative.

Architect or designer: Mackenzie & Moncur Ltd for the circa-1907 glasshouses.

The estate was acquired by Lord Keith in 1798. The castle later served as headquarters for the Free Polish Forces and has housed the Scottish Police College since 1954.

Architect or designer: William Atkinson.

The monument was scheduled in 1920. Its history includes medieval fortification, later hall-house development and substantial later alterations before abandonment.

The landscape later became the setting of the Scottish Police College. The official inventory polygon must be imported from HES.

Use the official GDL00379 polygon and link each listed or scheduled component as a separate feature.

features.name: Tulliallan Castle, Scottish Police College
features.statutoryStatus: Multiple statutory assets and inventory landscape
features.shortDescription: A Category A castellated Gothic mansion built for Admiral Lord Keith, now at the heart of the Scottish Police College.
features.fullDescription:
The estate was acquired by Lord Keith in 1798. The castle later served as headquarters for the Free Polish Forces and has housed the Scottish Police College since 1954.

Architect or designer: William Atkinson.

The monument was scheduled in 1920. Its history includes medieval fortification, later hall-house development and substantial later alterations before abandonment.
